title: Wide-Mass-Scanning-Range Setup and Phase-Resolved Protocol for Axion Dark Matter Detection
abstract: We propose a paradigm for quantum enhanced axion dark matter search, which does not rely on power measurements. We propose to measure directly the axion amplitude and phase in an interferometric protocol at the quantum limit, using a non-linear cavity. In addition, we introduce gyromagnetic modes as wide mass range transducers for axion signals compatible with standard haloscope designs. We expect this scheme to offer an improvement of at least 4 orders of magnitude in figure of merit and at least 2 orders of magnitude in mass window with respect to standard haloscopes. Owing to its generality, our proposed protocol has the potential to speed up axion search but also the search for dark photons or other cosmological objects, such as galactic masers.
summary: This paper proposes a breakthrough detection method for axion dark matter using a phase-resolved haloscope. Instead of measuring excess power, the technique measures the phase shift induced by the axion field via coupling to a tunable gyromagnetic mode. This approach promises significantly enhanced sensitivity and a vastly expanded search range compared to current state-of-the-art detectors.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a quantum-enhanced, phase-resolved protocol for detecting extremely weak axion dark matter signals, overcoming the limitations of conventional power-measurement haloscopes.
main_result: The proposed phase-resolved haloscope technique promises improvements of at least 4 orders of magnitude in figure of merit and 2 orders of magnitude in mass window compared to standard haloscopes.
method: The method involves measuring the axion amplitude and phase directly using an interferometric protocol, which translates the axion interaction into a measurable frequency shift rather than just an excess power.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a non-linear cavity coupled to a magnetic crystal hosting 'gyromagnetic modes' ($\hat{m}$). The dynamics are analyzed using the Keldysh path integral technique to derive an effective action for the readout mode.
key_observables: The key observable is the phase shift (frequency shift, $\Delta\omega_a$) in the readout cavity, which depends on the phase difference between the axion and the gyromagnetic mode.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the axion-photon coupling constant ($g_{a\gamma\gamma}$), the coupling strengths ($K_{am}$), and the achievable figure of merit ($F_{phase}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the semiclassical approximation and assumes the gyromagnetic mode is hosted by a magnetic chiral crystal like YIG.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between conventional (power-based) and phase-resolved (phase-based) haloscopes, showing the superior sensitivity and tunability of the proposed method.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general Hamiltonian, then deriving the phase-resolved signal mechanism via the Keldysh path integral, and finally quantifying the performance improvement by comparing the figure of merit ($F_{phase}$) against conventional benchmarks.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it proposes a novel measurement scheme that moves beyond simple power detection to utilize phase information in a superconducting cavity QED setup.
